> Hi Alex — thanks for the clear redline and timeline. We can take this on but need to coordinate across Legal and Implementation.

Alex / Soojin — reviewed the HF_OrderForm_v3_redline. Two quick notes from a legal perspective:

1) Rollback clause: we can accept a rollback path, but we need to preserve a minimum contractual commitment to avoid revenue and provisioning churn. Suggested compromise: allow the rollback after a defined notice window but maintain a fee floor equal to 25% of the original committed spend for the duration of the rollback plus a 3-month true-up period. This prevents perpetual degradation while giving Helium breathing room.

2) Split carve-up: we can document the 50/50 capacity split in an exhibit and keep a single order form. However, the fallback language must include an explicit owner for cross-BU disputes and an ops handback procedure.

3) Fee floor removal: I do not recommend a full removal. If Helium insists on waiver, we will require an alternative commercial offset (e.g., shorter initial term or higher per-token unit price for the split capacity months).

I've attached a marked-up legal redline with suggested wording (see Redwood_legal_carveup_comments.pdf). If the customer is willing to accept a 25% fee floor plus a 3-month true-up, legal is prepared to sign off quickly and Laura (legal) can prepare the change order language for execution.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts — Redwood Inference

> Alex / Soojin — reviewed the HF_OrderForm_v3_redline. Two quick notes from a legal perspective:

Thanks — quick operational read from my side:
- Carve-up: we can implement a logical carve-up within the provisioning layer and tag usage per BU. It will add a small amount of orchestration complexity (billing tags, separate quota pools). We recommend a staged rollout: Week 1–4: mirror production traffic to new BU tags (no billing change) for verification; Week 5: flip billing to carved split; Week 6–8: monitor for steady state.
- Rollback: to avoid provisioning thrash, rollback should be executed only after two consecutive monthly checks and require a 14-day notice window. If rollback occurs, proration will apply on a daily basis for the month of change; true-ups will be applied in the next invoice cycle.
- Billing/proration: proration will use daily token consumption as the basis; we will generate a separate invoice line for each BU for clarity.

I attached an Implementation-Matrix that lays out tasks, owners, and estimated hours. Ops is fine to support the carve-up provided we agree the acceptance criteria listed in the matrix.

Connor O'Brien
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
